analysis: The PR modifies only docs/threat-model.yaml. Added content at head: a header comment (lines 43-45), asset A-018 provider_serving_availability (lines 233-241), and, per the patch excerpt, new TB-012 (local add-on hold socket) plus T-059 around head lines 811-841 and 2305-2337. No executable code changed, and no existing controls, mitigations or open_findings were altered. I reviewed the supplied base unit (base lines 1874-2260, T-047 through T-058) and head unit (head lines 1-472). Those cover the header, the A-018 addition, TB-002 and TB-003, and none of the pre-existing entries were modified. The existing T-053, T-054 and T-057 text is unchanged and its authorization/final-writer claims are preserved. No regression or invalidated threat assumption is visible in the supplied text. Coverage limits: the TB-012 and T-059 bodies (head lines ~811-841 and ~2305-2337) were not supplied in full, because the patch excerpt is truncated and the head unit stops at line 472. I could not verify their claims about the signature check, leases, machine-lock fallback, same-user socket trust, or the busy-field handling that the PR defers to separate platform work. The A-018 note cites provider-swift/Sources/ProviderCore/Addon/ProviderLoop+AddonHold.swift, which is outside the supplied evidence. Questions for the next pass: (1) Does the hold socket authenticate the peer beyond same-UID, since a same-user local process could force a hold and cause a provider DoS (A-018)? (2) Is a hold ever able to bypass or extend App Attest authorization (A-016)? (3) Does the coordinator treat busy fields as untrusted provider-controlled input? These are unverified contracts, not findings.
